audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] says 'Full-build Malphite is barely touched by Subjugate's AD-steal payoff because he builds armor and AP, not AD.' Subjugate has no AD component at all, and the sentence concludes the exact opposite of the truth.
audit.why: Subjugate steals Health, Armor and Magic Resistance and doubles the theft over four seconds. Armour is the one stat Malphite has most of, and Ground Slam's damage is calculated from his Armor — so casting R on him removes his defence and his damage in the same instant. The entry has confused Subjugate with Chomp, which does sap Attack Damage and which really is close to worthless here. Getting these the wrong way round tells the player to stop using their single best tool into this matchup.
audit.corrected: Chomp's AD sap earns almost nothing here — Thunderclap's aftershocks and Ground Slam scale off Armor and ability power. Subjugate is the opposite: it takes the Armor his damage is calculated from.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (R Subjugate: Health, Armor and Magic Resistance, doubled over 4s; Q Chomp saps Attack Damage)
champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (E Ground Slam: 'deals magic damage based on his Armor')

audit.whatIsWrong: late tells the player to 'avoid him without Subjugate up — he will all-in you with Flash plus Unstoppable Force and you have no answer', and whys[4] says he 'can safely ignore your pattern when his cooldown is hidden'. Neither ultimate is ever given a number.
audit.why: The numbers reverse the framing. Subjugate is 120/100/80; Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100. Trundle's ultimate is back first at every single rank and the gap widens to 80 seconds against 100. So the side-lane window is not something Trundle has to wait for — it is structurally his. The real risk is a Flash-Unstoppable Force he never saw coming, which is a vision and positioning problem, not a cooldown one. This is the same correction the mirror audit made from Malphite's side, restated here.
audit.corrected: Subjugate 120/100/80 against Unstoppable Force 130/115/100 — yours is up first at every rank, widening to 80 against 100. The danger is a Flash-R from fog, not the timer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard is called 'annoying poke' twice and whys[3] claims 'Malphite stacks armor through Seismic Shard poke'. Ground Slam and Thunderclap are never named anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Seismic Shard grants no armour — it 'deals damage upon impact and steals Move Speed for 3 seconds', on a flat 8s at 625 range. That makes it the precise counter to the one thing Frozen Domain gives Trundle in lane, which the entry leans on repeatedly without ever mentioning the tool that erases it. Ground Slam is worse for Trundle and also unnamed: a flat 7s whose damage is calculated from Malphite's Armor and which cuts attack speed — and attack speed is what Frozen Domain buys and what Chomp's attack reset rides on. Thunderclap is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8 with an attack reset and on-hit aftershocks.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard is a flat 8s at 625 range that steals your move speed for three seconds — the direct answer to Frozen Domain. Ground Slam is a flat 7s calculated from his Armor that cuts your attack speed.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (Q cd 8 range 625 'stealing Move Speed for 3 seconds'; E cd 7 'based on his Armor... reduces the Attack Speed'; W cd 10/9.5/9/8.5/8, autoReset, onHit)

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart hands Trundle five of seven stages (Trundle, Trundle, Trundle, Skill, Trundle, Skill, Trundle) while the entry's own prose says the opposite from Level 6 onward: late opens 'Past first item Malphite wins this', whys[4] describes losing the all-in, whys[5] says 'he wins the war of attrition', whys[6] says his R 'is worth more than any split-push edge Trundle holds'. The full layer calls the matchup HARD and then report[14] calls it 'Favoured'.
audit.why: Three sources agree against the chart: the packet's 48.11% over 424 games, MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.malphite at 43.88, and the mirror audit, which concluded Trundle owns Levels 1 through 5 and Malphite owns Level 6 onward. The entry's prose already says exactly that. Only the enum values disagree, so this is a straight data error rather than a judgement call, and mirror-fix.js would rewrite it anyway.
audit.corrected: Trundle owns Level 1 through Levels 4-5; Malphite owns Level 6, first item and two-plus items — matching the prose, the 48.11% headline and the mirror.

audit.why: The entry's best original idea is right and worth keeping: the level 1-2 plan is to keep Granite Shield drained rather than to force a kill. Riot's text supports it — the shield absorbs damage up to 10% of Malphite's maximum health and only recharges 'if Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds'. Chomp's flat 3.5s at 300 range is exactly the tool for denying those seconds, so the advice and the cooldown fit together; I only added the numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] says Malphite should 'Save Unstoppable Force until Trundle commits Subjugate, then interrupt the drain window and reset the trade'.
audit.why: Subjugate steals immediately and then doubles the amount over the next four seconds. Riot's text describes no channel and no maintained condition, so there is no 'drain window' for a knock-up to interrupt. What Unstoppable Force actually does to Trundle is land a displacement he carries nothing to break — no dash, no stun, no untargetability — with only Pillar of Ice's terrain on a 21-second cooldown as an approximation of an answer. That is the version of the threat the player should be planning around.
audit.corrected: Unstoppable Force lands because Trundle carries no dash and no stun to break it — only Pillar of Ice terrain on 21s. The theft itself is instant, then doubles over four seconds.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (R Subjugate; no dash or hardCC in kit)

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are genuinely even — Chomp's AD steal hurts Malphite but his passive armor shield absorbs the burst, so don't over-commit early trying to smash him. Last-hit with Chomp and let his shield stay down between your bites; if he steps up to poke, hit him once, refresh the AD steal, and let the shield work for you by keeping it drained. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain the instant he trades back — the movement speed gap lets you land an extra auto inside the zone that he cannot match without burning Flash. The goal these early levels is not a kill; it is keeping his passive shield on cooldown so level 3 finds him without it.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are genuinely even — Chomp bites every 3.5s, but Granite Shield absorbs up to a tenth of his maximum health, so don't over-commit trying to smash him. Last-hit with Chomp and keep that shield drained: it only recharges once he has gone a few seconds without being hit, and a 3.5s bite is how you deny those seconds. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain the instant he trades back — the movement gap buys you an extra auto inside the zone. Watch for Seismic Shard, a flat 8s at 625 range that steals your move speed for three seconds; that is his answer to the zone. The goal is arriving at level 3 with his shield still down.

edits.before: Level 3 is your best solo window and you need to take it — Q into Frozen Domain, chase with the movement speed boost, and Pillar behind him so he cannot simply walk out. If that trade goes well, look for a short extended trade at 4-5: Malphite's Seismic Shard poke is annoying but Chomp's sustain-negation and your W healing eat a lot of it. Do not stand in his Seismic Shard path trying to last-hit — dodge it and then step forward for a Chomp, not the reverse. Level 6 shifts the dynamic: his Unstoppable Force is now a genuine threat even in lane if he decides to flash-R you under tower. Respect it — trade only when you know its cooldown, and if you must all-in, land Pillar first to cut off his dash angle so your Subjugate lands before he can escape the zone.
edits.after: Level 3 is your best solo window and you need to take it — Q into Frozen Domain, chase on the movement speed, and Pillar behind him so he cannot simply walk out. If that goes well, look for a short extended trade at 4-5: Seismic Shard poke from 625 range is annoying, but the bigger problem is Ground Slam, a flat 7s whose damage is calculated from his Armor and whose attack-speed cut blunts the bite cadence Frozen Domain paid for. Dodge the Shard, then step in for a Chomp, never the reverse. Level 6 shifts things, though not against you: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100 while Subjugate is 120/100/80, so yours is back first at every rank. Land Pillar first, then R, and keep the whole fight inside your own zone.

edits.before: Past first item Malphite wins this. His armor itemization makes Chomp's AD steal earn diminishing returns, his passive shield recharges before every trade, and one clean Unstoppable Force in a teamfight ends the fight before you Subjugate anything. Your late game value is entirely Subjugate into his biggest frontliner in 5v5: drain half his armor and magic resist, let your team walk through the shell. In the side lane avoid him without Subjugate up — he will all-in you with Flash plus Unstoppable Force and you have no answer. Split when he is elsewhere, recall and rotate the moment R is down, and let your team use the window you create by threatening the 1v1 rather than trying to actually take it.
edits.after: Past first item Malphite wins this. Armour makes him tougher and makes Ground Slam hit harder, since its damage is calculated from it, Granite Shield recharges before every trade, and one clean Unstoppable Force ends a teamfight. Chomp's AD sap earns almost nothing here — Thunderclap's aftershocks and Ground Slam are built on Armor and ability power, not attack damage. But your ultimate is the answer rather than the victim: Subjugate takes Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft across four seconds, and Armor is the stat his damage runs on. In the side lane engage on your own timer — 120/100/80 against his 130/115/100, so yours is up first — and rotate the moment his is back.

notes: MIRROR REUSED: audits/top/malphite__trundle.json already established the two decisive facts, and this entry states them from Trundle's side without re-deriving them — (a) Subjugate 120/100/80 beats Unstoppable Force 130/115/100 at every rank, widening to 80 against 100, and (b) Chomp's AD sap is close to worthless because Thunderclap's aftershocks and Ground Slam are calculated from Armor and ability power. BIGGEST CORRECTION: whys[6] said Subjugate barely touches a full-build Malphite 'because he builds armor and AP, not AD'. Subjugate has no AD component — it takes Health, Armor and MR, and Armor is precisely the stat Ground Slam's damage is calculated from, so R strips his defence and his damage at once. The entry had swapped Subjugate and Chomp and, in doing so, told the player to stop using their best tool. SECOND CORRECTION: 'Malphite stacks armor through Seismic Shard poke' — Seismic Shard grants no armour; it steals MOVE SPEED for three seconds on a flat 8s at 625 range, which makes it the direct counter to Frozen Domain, the thing this entry leans on hardest. Added Ground Slam (flat 7s, damage from Armor, attack-speed cut) and Thunderclap (10/9.5/9/8.5/8, attack reset, on-hit aftershocks); neither was named anywhere in either layer. THIRD: wants.foe[1] had Malphite 'interrupting the drain window' of Subjugate — the theft is instant and then doubles over four seconds, with no channel to break; what actually lands is a knock-up Trundle carries nothing to answer except Pillar terrain on 21s. CHART EDITED: unusually, I did change the enums here, because it is not a judgement call — the packet (48.11% over 424 games), MC_WR_TABLES (43.88), the mirror audit and the entry's own prose all say Malphite owns Level 6 onward, while only the enum values disagreed. win[3] and phases[3].side to Trundle; win[4-6] and phases[4-6].side to Malphite. Also fixed report[14] calling it 'Favoured' while diff reads HARD. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: whether Pillar of Ice stops Unstoppable Force in flight — Riot's text calls the pillar impassable terrain and says nothing about interrupting a dash, so I kept the existing 'cut off his dash angle' phrasing and did not strengthen it.
